_doc: Task 6A section 4.1 preflight. Read-only survey of the machine BEFORE any environment change. Every value here is MEASURED on the host at 2026-09-26 unless a field says otherwise.

python.note: System Python is left untouched. All Task 6A work happens in a new dedicated conda environment.

existing_torch_reference_measurement._doc: Measured by importing torch from the pre-existing yolo_sam_env. That environment was READ ONLY and is not modified by Task 6A. Basis for choosing the new environment's wheel family.

system_cuda.consequence: The optional SAM2 CUDA extension (sam2._C) cannot be compiled on this host. Task 6A therefore intentionally installs SAM2 with SAM2_BUILD_CUDA=0, which the official project documents as supported and which only disables mask hole/sprinkle post-processing.

disk.sufficiency_assessment: Sufficient for Task 6A. Estimated new consumption: PyTorch CUDA wheels ~3.5 GB, dependency stack ~1.5 GB, conda environment ~2 GB, Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct ~4.0 GB, sam2.1-hiera-base-plus ~0.6 GB, SAM2 source <0.1 GB, caches/artifacts ~2 GB => roughly 14 GB of the 77.5 GB free.
disk.reason_not_more: The reviewer's earlier note that 250-300 GB could be freed refers to potential cleanup that has not been performed; Task 6A does not delete unrelated files.

cache_environment_variables.note: None were set at preflight. Task 6A sets project-local cache paths process-locally (not system-wide) so that downloads stay inside the repository's ignored local_cache/ directory.

network_reachability_note.observed: The Windows hosts file contains a Steam++ / Watt Toolkit blocklist mapping github.com and huggingface.co to 127.0.0.1, but a local listener transparently proxies those connections, so ordinary HTTP clients (Python, pip, git) reach them.
network_reachability_note.consequence: Weight and package downloads are expected to work; if they do not, the ModelScope route is the documented fallback for Qwen models.
